records.title: Virtual Cockpit Display Failure and Black Screen
records.description: The Audi Virtual Cockpit digital instrument cluster can experience intermittent black screens, pixelation, or complete display failure. The NVIDIA Tegra processor overheats or the display connection becomes loose. Some units fail from software corruption during OTA updates. The issue leaves drivers without speedometer, fuel gauge, and warning indicators.
records.solution: First attempt a system reset by holding the ignition off for 5 minutes. If the issue persists, the instrument cluster needs to be replaced or repaired. Some independent shops can reflow solder connections for $300-$500 vs. $2,000+ dealer replacement. A software update from Audi may resolve intermittent blackout issues.
symptoms: Instrument cluster goes completely black while driving
Display shows pixelated or garbled graphics
No speedometer or gauge readings displayed
Warning chimes without visible warnings on display

communityRecommendations.content: Before paying for a new cluster, try disconnecting the 12V battery for 30 minutes. This forces a full system reset and resolves software-related blackouts in about 40% of cases per Audizine reports.
Check if your VIN has a pending software campaign by calling Audi Customer Care at 1-800-822-2834. Many Virtual Cockpit issues are covered under a silent recall/campaign.
A failed instrument cluster is a safety issue — no speedometer, no fuel gauge, no warning lights. Do not delay repair. Use a phone GPS speedometer app as a temporary workaround while awaiting parts.

records.title: Connecting Rod Bearing Failure (NHTSA Recall 22V753000)
records.description: Deviations in the mechanical production of the connecting rods left increased metal-particle contamination in the engine oil circuit on early Q5 Sportback models. This causes accelerated wear and excessive bearing play, which can spin/damage a connecting rod bearing and lead to catastrophic engine failure. If the failure breaches the block it can leak oil and create a fire risk. Recall 22V753000 (Audi code 13I5) covers 2021-2023 Q5 and Q5 Sportback Quattro vehicles.
records.solution: Under the safety recall, the dealer inspects the engine and replaces the affected engine free of charge if damage is found. Owners should verify recall completion by VIN; outside of the recall, a spun-bearing engine typically requires a long-block or complete engine replacement.

records.title: EA888 Water Pump / Thermostat Housing Coolant Leak (45 TFSI)
records.description: The combined plastic water pump and thermostat housing on the EA888 Gen 3 2.0T (45 TFSI) is a well-documented weak point shared across the B9 Audi range (Q5, A4, A5). The plastic housing becomes brittle from repeated heat cycling and cracks at the seal/weep area, causing a slow coolant loss that often shows no obvious puddle. Left unaddressed it can lead to overheating and, in some cases, electrical shorts from coolant intrusion. Failures are reported as early as ~4 years / 50,000-60,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the water pump and integrated thermostat housing as an assembly (standard practice is to do both together), ideally with an upgraded/revised unit. Refill and bleed the cooling system. Audi has covered some affected pumps under goodwill/warranty extension in certain markets.

records.title: Excessive Engine Oil Consumption (2.0 TFSI EA888)
records.description: Audi's EA888 2.0 TFSI engines are prone to elevated oil consumption. Low-tension oil-control piston rings with small drain-back holes can become clogged with carbon, trapping oil on the cylinder walls where it burns. German owners on motor-talk's Q5 FY forum report roughly 0.5 L consumed per ~7,500 km, and many owners are forced to top up between services. Direct injection compounds the problem with intake-valve carbon buildup over time.
records.solution: Confirm consumption with a documented Audi oil-consumption test. Remedies range from PCV/oil-separator service and updated piston rings to, in severe cases, piston/ring replacement; walnut-blasting addresses associated intake-valve carbon. Owners should monitor oil level frequently between service intervals as a safeguard.

records.title: Front Assist Phantom Braking / False Emergency Braking (ADAS)
records.description: Q5 owners report the Front Assist / pre sense automatic emergency braking system triggering sudden, forceful braking at speed with no real obstacle present ('phantom braking'), creating a rear-end collision risk. Conversely, some report the ADAS failing to give pre-sense warnings when a genuine hazard exists. Complaints are logged with NHTSA across 2021-2025 model years and are linked to radar/camera sensor or software calibration issues.
records.solution: Have the dealer scan for ADAS faults and apply any available radar/camera control-module software updates and sensor recalibration; check for and clear obstructions/misalignment of the front radar. Persistent cases may require sensor replacement. Document incidents and file an NHTSA complaint, as ongoing investigations can drive a recall.

records.title: Loose Cylinder Head Cover Screws Causing Oil Leak and Fire Risk (Recall 25V294)
records.description: Cylinder head cover (valve cover) screws were improperly torqued at the factory and, on some units, featured burrs that could damage the cylinder head. The screws can loosen over time, allowing engine oil to leak onto hot engine components and increasing the risk of an underhood fire. NHTSA recall 25V294 (Audi code 15ZK) covers roughly 89,000-106,000 2022-2024 Q5 Quattro and Q5 Sportback Quattro vehicles; Audi estimates about 5% of the population had screws not properly torqued.
records.solution: Dealers inspect and re-torque or replace the cylinder head cover screws (and inspect the cover/head for damage) free of charge under the recall. Owners noticing burning-oil smell or oil residue around the valve cover should have it inspected immediately and confirm recall status by VIN.

records.title: Mild Hybrid (MHEV) Electrical Fault and Start-Stop Failure
records.description: The Q5 Sportback's 12V mild-hybrid system uses both a main AGM battery and a 12V lithium-ion auxiliary battery (trunk-mounted) feeding a belt alternator-starter. Owners report 'Electrical system malfunction' messages, non-functional start-stop, and lost-communication faults with the DC-DC converter or battery energy control modules. Weak/aging auxiliary batteries and converter faults are common triggers, often worse in cold weather.
records.solution: Diagnose with Audi ODIS to identify the faulting module; remedies include replacing the 12V lithium-ion auxiliary battery and/or main AGM battery, re-coding/registering the new battery, and updating affected control-module software. Audi has contributed to repair costs in some documented cases.

records.title: PHEV High-Voltage Battery Overheating / Fire Risk (Recall 25V080000)
records.description: On Q5 55 TFSI e quattro plug-in hybrid models, defective Samsung SDI high-voltage battery cells/modules can overheat and present a fire risk, even when parked or charging. Affected vehicles were built between August 2021 and December 2022. NHTSA recall 25V080000 covers 2021-2024 Q5 PHEV (TFSI e) models. As an interim measure Audi pushed a software update to monitor battery temperature, and owners of unmonitored vehicles were told not to charge until the final remedy.
records.solution: Audi installs advanced diagnostic/monitoring software as the final remedy and replaces individual battery modules or the entire high-voltage pack where defective cells are detected, free of charge. Affected owners should follow the do-not-charge guidance until inspected and confirm recall status by VIN.

records.title: Rear Brake Squeal and Premature Pad Wear
records.description: The Q5 Sportback rear brakes develop persistent squealing, especially at low speeds and during light braking. The OEM brake pads have a metallic compound that resonates against the rear rotors. Additionally, the electronic parking brake auto-applies frequently, causing accelerated rear pad wear. Rear pads may wear out by 20,000-25,000 miles vs. the expected 40,000+.
records.solution: Replace rear brake pads with aftermarket ceramic compound pads that eliminate the metallic resonance squeal. Apply brake pad shims and caliper slide pin lubricant. Have the electronic parking brake calibrated via scan tool to reduce unnecessary auto-apply frequency. Replace rotors if they show scoring or are below minimum thickness.
symptoms: High-pitched squealing from rear brakes at low speed
Rear brake pads worn significantly more than fronts
Grinding noise when brakes are cold
Brake dust buildup on rear wheels significantly more than front
Parking brake warning light appearing intermittently

communityRecommendations.content: Akebono Euro Ceramic rear pads (EUR1547) completely eliminate the squeal. They produce less dust and last longer than OEM pads. Widely recommended on Audizine Q5 forums.
Apply CRC Disc Brake Quiet (copper paste) to the back of the pads during installation. This dampens the vibration that causes squealing.
After pad replacement, perform 10 moderate stops from 35 mph to properly bed the new pads. Improper bedding is the #1 cause of new pads squealing.

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Wind Noise and Rattle
records.description: The panoramic sunroof develops rattling noises at highway speeds and wind noise around the leading edge seal. The sunroof glass deflector can also come loose or break. More noticeable in cold weather when seals contract.
records.solution: Clean and lubricate sunroof rails and seals with Krytox or silicone grease. Adjust sunroof alignment via dealer. Replace wind deflector if cracked. In some cases, the sunroof cassette requires re-indexing via scan tool.
